direct_answer: The NHS App and practice online services let you order prescriptions, view records and contact your GP. Family can help through proxy access. For urgent problems, use NHS 111 or 999.
author: Louis Maxwell
keywords: NHS App, online GP, remote consultation, proxy access, arthritis, frailty, UK
content:
Online access can save tiring trips.

This guide covers using it. It is educational information, not a diagnosis or personal treatment plan.

What you can do

  • Order repeats.
  • View records.
  • Contact your practice.

Proxy access

Family or carers can be given access with permission.

When to call instead

Use NHS 111 or 999 for urgent problems.

When to get help

  • Call 999 or go to A&E if someone suddenly becomes confused. Many causes need immediate assessment. Do not assume it is a urine infection, dementia or a medicine effect. Do not drive yourself to A&E; ask someone else to drive or call 999. Stay with the person and reassure them while help is arranged.
  • Call 999 for chest pain, trouble breathing, signs of a stroke, or a fall with a possible serious injury.
  • Get urgent advice the same day (NHS 111 or your GP) for a sudden drop in mobility or a hot, swollen joint with fever.
  • See your GP for a steady decline over weeks, unplanned weight loss or repeated falls.

Never stop or change a prescribed medicine yourself. Ask your GP or pharmacist for a review.

Common questions

Do I need a smartphone?

A computer also works.

Is it safe?

Keep login details private.

Educational information for people in the United Kingdom — not a diagnosis or personal medical advice. Charity no. 1218461. Living With Arthritis is an independent charity and is not part of Arthritis UK (formerly Versus Arthritis). Everyone's situation is different, so follow the advice of your own GP and care team. If you feel very unwell, call 999 or go to A&E. For urgent advice, contact NHS 111 (NHS 24 on 111 in Scotland; in Northern Ireland, your GP or GP out-of-hours service).
